```python
from typing import List


def parse_music(music_string: str) -> List[int]:
    
    note_map = {'o': 4, 'o|': 2, '.|': 1}
    return [note_map[x] for x in music_string.split(' ') if x]



# Unit test for function parse_music
def test_parse_music():
    # Empty string yields no beats
    assert parse_music("") == []

    # Single whole note
    assert parse_music("o") == [4]

    # Single half note
    assert parse_music("o|") == [2]

    # Single quarter note
    assert parse_music(".|") == [1]

    # Mixed notes, one of each type
    assert parse_music("o o| .|") == [4, 2, 1]

    # Classic example: sequence of varying lengths
    assert parse_music("o o| .| o| o| .| .| .| .| o o") == [
        4, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 4, 4
    ]

    # Repeated quarter notes
    assert parse_music(".| .| .| .|") == [1, 1, 1, 1]

    # Extra whitespace between notes is ignored
    assert parse_music("  o   o|  ") == [4, 2]

    # Result length matches number of tokens
    result = parse_music("o o o o| .|")
    assert len(result) == 5

    # Sum of beats for a known melody
    melody = "o .| o| .|"
    assert sum(parse_music(melody)) == 8

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_parse_music()
```

```python
def test_parse_music():
```

```python
    assert parse_music('o|') == [2]
    assert parse_music('.|') == [1]

    # Mixed notes
    assert parse_music('o o| .|') == [4, 2, 1]

    # Classic example sequence
    assert parse_music('o o| .| o| o| .| .| .| .| o o') == [4, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 4, 4]

    assert parse_music(' o ') == [4]
    assert parse_music('   ') == []

    # Repeated notes
    assert parse_music('.| .| .| .|') == [1, 1, 1, 1]
    assert parse_music('o| o| o|') == [2, 2, 2]
    assert parse_music('o o o') == [4, 4, 4]

    # Alternating pattern
    assert parse_music('o .| o .|') == [4, 1, 4, 1]

    # Long sequence
    assert parse_music('o| .| o .| o| .| o') == [2, 1, 4, 1, 2, 1, 4]
```
